Things about this data that need to be cleaned up; Conversion of VALUES to NA & Split Tag \#

Column Separation,

We need rows for each planted acorn that did not germinate, this would create more NAs but summaries would make much more sense.

To import and merge spreadsheets;

```{r}
install.packages("plyr") #contains the lapply function
library("dplyr")
library("plyr")
library("readr")
library("readxl")

```

```{r}
oak_data <- list.files(path = "Oak Project/Data",
                       pattern = "*6Clean.xlsx",
                       full.names = TRUE) |> #asking all files that have a pattern, we are excluding OCT2025
  lapply(read_excel,
         na = "NA", sheet = "Input1", skip = 1) |> 
  bind_rows()
#Takes four seperate data sheets and staples them together in one datasheet, lines columns together
#takes the excel sheet and applies it to all files 
names(oak_data)
unloadNamespace("plyr")
```

```{r}
oak_data <-
  oak_data |> 
dplyr:: rename(Page_Num ="Page #", 
                       Date = "MM/DD/YYYY",
                       Recorder ="Name",
                       Block ="#...4",
                       Tag_Num ="#...5",
                       Oak_Type ="NR, S, or A",
                       Treatment ="AC, OA, NP, DT, or DL",
                       OA_microclimate ="TH, TI, CN",
                       Seedling_Ht_Cm ="(cm)",
                       Num_Leaves ="#...10",
                       Num_Dead_Leaves ="#...11",
                       Leaf_Greenness ="%",
                       Num_Germinated ="#...13",
                       RCD ="(mm)",
                       Notes  ="as written on data sheet")

oak_data
```

```{r}
view(oak_data)
```

```{r}
oak_data_CLEAN <- oak_data |> 
  separate ('Tag_Num', into = c("Tag_Num", "Acorn_Num"), sep = "A") |> 
  mutate(Tag_Num = as.numeric(Tag_Num)) |> 
  mutate(Acorn_Num = as.numeric(Acorn_Num)) |> 
  
  mutate(Leaf_Greenness = as.numeric(Leaf_Greenness),
         Dead = case_when(
           Seedling_Ht_Cm == 0 ~ "Dead",
           Seedling_Ht_Cm > 0 ~ "Alive"
         )) ##VALUES TO NA, case when = if then  
#
oak_data_CLEAN
#Breaks up the original tag number oclumn into tag number and acorn nuber by seperating by A. 
#mutate makes new columns, can change exisiting columns
#This good, continue cleaning from this
# ' = if column name has a space between, it keeps the words together 
```

```{r}
oak_data_CLEAN |> 
  select(Tag_Num, Acorn_Num) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  arrange(Tag_Num)

Acorn_ID_Table <- oak_data_CLEAN |> 
  select(Tag_Num, Block, Treatment, OA_microclimate, Date) |> 
  distinct() |> 
  arrange(Tag_Num) |> 
  mutate(Acorn1 = 1, Acorn2 = 2, Acorn3 = 3) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols  = c(Acorn1, Acorn2, Acorn3),
    names_to = "whatever",
    values_to = "Acorn_Num") |> 
  select(-whatever)
view(oak_data_CLEAN)
```

CONTINUED DATA CLEANING:

```{r}
#Need to isolate all the different treatments from everything else in the dataset.
#The isolation of treatments are made into separate datasets for analysis. 
#NAs need to be removed for both height & greenness.
Height_Green_RCD <- oak_data_CLEAN |> 
  filter(Treatment == "DT"|
         Treatment == "AC"|
         Treatment == "OA")
# NA removal for height and greeness; The filter function is filtering for the seedling ht to be greater than 0, this helps to filter out the NAs. Look at the data itself will help to determine how to exactly filter out numerics. 
#The mutate function works to make sure that leaf greenness is being read as a numeric.  
Height_Green_RCD <- Height_Green_RCD |> 
  filter(Seedling_Ht_Cm > 0) |> 
  mutate(Leaf_Greenness = as.numeric(Leaf_Greenness))

#Need to separate the natural recruits and acorns now into two separate, that making new datasets for both and filtering oak type. 

Acorn_Data <- Height_Green_RCD |> 
  filter(Oak_Type == "A")

NR_Data <- Height_Green_RCD |> 
  filter(Oak_Type == "NR" )

#The acorn data has NAs for RCD & Greenness In order to remove those NAs, in this case we want to change the NAs into 0. In order to do that, the function mutate can be used to specifically change the NAs to 0 in specified columns

Acorn_Clean <- Acorn_Data |> 
  mutate(Leaf_Greenness = ifelse(is.na(Leaf_Greenness), 0, Leaf_Greenness),
         RCD = ifelse(is.na(RCD), 0, RCD) )
#There was no NAs present in the NR Data, so that data set is good. 

#The data has now been "cleaned" and separated between acorns and NR. 

#At this point, data is cleaned and it is time to explore with analysis. 
```

```{r}
#This is data exploration of figuring out how to do a time series with the NR data
qplot(x=Date, y=Seedling_Ht_Cm,
      data=NR_Data, na.rm=TRUE,
      main="Seedling Height Over Time of Natural Recruits",
      xlab="Date", ylab="Seedling Height (cm)")

ggplot(data = NR_Data, aes(x = Date, y = Seedling_Ht_Cm)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Seedling Height over Time (NR)", x = "Date", y = "Seedling Height")

ggplot(data = NR_Data, aes(x = Date, y = RCD)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "RCD over Time (NR)", x = "Date", y = "RCD")

ggplot(data = NR_Data, aes(x = Date, y = Leaf_Greenness)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Leaf Greenness over Time (NR)", x = "Date", y = "Leaf Greenness")

ggplot(NR_Data, aes(x = Date, y = Seedling_Ht_Cm, color = Tag_Num, group = Tag_Num)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(title = "Seedling Ht for NR over Time",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Seedling Height",
       color = "Tag") +
  theme_minimal()

#Try to facet wrap! to divide by treatment
```

## Two Way ANOVA

The two-way factorial design has TWO categorical predictor variables and ONE response, and you are interested in interactions between the two predictor variables.

Example: How do temperature (hi, med, lo) and acidity (more acidic, more basic) affect algal photosynthesis rates?
